//: Story Phase 3, chapter 10: Blackbeard Becomes Stinkbeard. Still the same evening. Garrick's amendment is nailed to the mainmast (read from (9,21)/(10,21)); the confrontation happens at his barrel (11,16). From captain_named_stinkbeard onward the captain's name plate, status page, save slots and {captain} all read Stinkbeard.
p3c2.begin: wick[alarmed]: Captain! Captain, you'd better see the mainmast.
captain: What's wrong with the mainmast?
wick[concerned]: Nothing's wrong with the MAST. It's what's nailed to it.
wick: I think it's about you, Captain. I only read the first line. I didn't like the first line.
p3c2.notice: A sheet of good paper, nailed to the mainmast with four nails, one of them a fork.

p3c2.notice.caption: Nailed to the mainmast. The ink is still wet. So, somehow, is the paper.

p3c2.notice.tutorial: Garrick is waiting at his barrel. Have a word with him about the amendment.
p3c2.notice.title: What Did You Call Me?

start: garrick[businesslike]: A provisional rebrand, Captain. Pending your approval.
garrick[smug]: Which I've taken the liberty of pre-approving, to save you the paperwork.
captain[angry]: My name is BLACKBEARD. It has been Blackbeard for twenty years. Ports close when they hear it.
garrick: And that's the problem, Captain. It's out of date.
A crowd has gathered. It always does, now, wherever Garrick is. Partly to see what he'll do. Mostly to see where he'll do it.
garrick[businesslike]: Captain. This morning, you went into the Dead Center of the cloud. For the bird.
garrick: A tremendous act of courage. I've said so in the log.
garrick: But you didn't go in alone, Captain. Your beard went in with you.
garrick[proud]: A big, black, heroic beard. And it's been soaking up the product ever since. Like a sponge.
captain: My beard does not smell.
garrick: With respect, Captain, you've been standing in it all afternoon. You wouldn't know.
rook[concerned]: He's got a point, Cap'n. Just a little sniff. To settle it.

then: captain[angry]: I am NOT smelling my own beard in front of the crew.
Nobody says anything. Nobody moves. Everyone is looking at the beard.
Squawks has no feathers left on his head, and he is still, somehow, raising an eyebrow.
else: The crew wait. They have all evening. You, it turns out, have rather less.

sniff: You lift the end of your beard, very slowly, toward your nose.
captain[queasy]: Hhhk—
captain[coughing]: *HACK* *KOFF* Oh— oh, SEA and STARS—
gristle[alarmed]: He's gone GREEN.
hale[alarmed]: Captain? Captain, sit down—
captain[coughing]: I'm FINE. I'm— *hkk*— the eyes. Why is it in my EYES?
garrick[proud]: Ah. You'll be getting the top notes now, Captain. Old rum. Sea salt. A little gunpowder. Very traditional.
garrick: Then the middle notes. Wet dog. Burnt onion. A hint of Dead Center.
rook[queasy]: It has MIDDLE NOTES?
garrick[businesslike]: And the finish, Rook. It lingers. Like a good dinner guest.
captain[queasy]: ...It's still going.
garrick: That's the finish.
garrick[proud]: Captain. I've classified a great many smells today. I don't say this lightly.
garrick: This is not a scent.
garrick[businesslike]: This is an attack.
captain[angry]: It doesn't matter. It'll wash out. And my name is Blackbeard.
garrick: Stinkbeard.
captain[angry]: BLACKBEARD.
garrick[smug]: Stinkbeard.
captain[angry]: BLACK.
garrick: Stink.
captain[angry]: BLACK!
garrick[proud]: STINK!
captain[angry]: I will NOT be called Stinkbeard by a man wearing the galley curtain!
garrick[pretend]: Captain, I don't want this to become unpleasant.
Every single person on deck stops breathing at once. Gristle, who had only just started again, makes a small, sad noise.
squawks[horrified]: DEADLY BR—
captain[alarmed]: Not YET, Squawks!
garrick[businesslike]: I had the second helping of Jim's bean stew, Captain. For morale.
garrick: And a man under a great deal of stress can't always be responsible for his digestion.
garrick[pretend]: Whereas a man whose ship has a properly registered captain feels very, very calm.
hale[alarmed]: Captain. Captain, the hatch is open. It'll go straight down to the hammocks.
wick[alarmed]: We only just got the hammocks back!
You look at the crew. Rook, with a sock on his face. Bob, breathing through a bottle. Gristle, blue around the lips.
You look at Squawks. He's shivering under his blanket. He has had a very long day.
captain[resigned]: ...Fine.
garrick[delighted]: Fine?
captain[resigned]: For the ship. Not for you. For the ship.

choice.text: "Write it down before I change my mind."
then: captain[resigned]: Write it down before I change my mind.
garrick[proud]: Already written, Captain! In ink! Say it, though. It's nicer when you say it.

sniff: garrick[delighted]: Captain Stinkbeard! Master of the Queen Anne's Revenge! Terror of the Sapphire Sea!
brask[surprised]: ...It's got a ring to it.
captain[angry]: It does NOT have a ring to it.
sully[happy]: It sort of does, Captain.
squawks[smug]: Beard.
squawks[smug]: Stinks.
captain[resigned]: Thank you, Squawks.
captain: Garrick. It washes out. Tell me it washes out.
garrick[businesslike]: Oh, certainly, Captain. In time. With the right approach.
garrick: The difficulty is that it's root-deep. You see, every great beard has a second beard, underneath.
garrick[proud]: The beard beneath the beard. And the product's got into that one too.
captain[angry]: That's nonsense.
garrick: This morning, Captain, you'd have said gold that smells worthless was nonsense.
captain: ...
captain[resigned]: How long?
garrick[businesslike]: Taking into account the depth of penetration, the density of the beard, the prevailing humidity...
garrick: ...Centuries. Give or take.
captain: CENTURIES?
garrick[pretend]: A short few centuries.
A fat drop of rain lands on your beard. Then another. Then the sky opens.
Somewhere in the beard beneath the beard, something wakes up and sighs.
garrick[businesslike]: Ah. Humidity.
garrick: ...I've extended the estimate.
